title: NFC Tag Manufacturer in China — Stickers & Inlays
summary: Proud Tek is a Shenzhen NFC tag manufacturer — building 13.56 MHz tags since 2008 and exporting to B2B buyers worldwide — that owns every step from antenna and chip bonding through converting, printing and encoding, so an NFC program is made on one line rather than assembled from five subcontractors. We manufacture the full form-factor range — paper and PET stickers, wet and dry inlays on converter rolls, epoxy hard tags, anti-metal tags and NTAG 424 DNA tamper-evident labels — on NTAG 213/215/216, NTAG 424 DNA, MIFARE Ultralight and ICODE SLIX2 silicon allocated directly from NXP. Because the line is ours, so is the customization: antenna geometry, chip choice, substrate, artwork, encoding and OEM/ODM branding are specified by you and read-verified by us before a carton ships. Below is the chip-and-form-factor menu we build, how a tag is made on the floor, and the certifications a procurement team can check before the first order.
heroPoints: Own-the-line manufacturing — antenna etching, flip-chip bonding, roll converting, printing and inline encoding all run in our Shenzhen factory, so nothing critical is farmed out to a job shop.
NXP-allocated silicon — NTAG 213/215/216, NTAG 424 DNA, MIFARE Ultralight and ICODE SLIX2 sourced through NXP and NXP-authorised distribution, so the chip in the tag is genuine, traceable silicon.
Built for OEM/ODM export — your artwork, antenna and encoding to spec, free sample kits, factory-direct pricing, and ISO 9001 / 14001 / 45001 certificates plus the paperwork customs asks for.

sections.title: Every NFC tag we ship is built on our own Shenzhen line
sections.intro: 'Made in China' hides a wide range — from a factory that bonds its own chips to a trading desk that photographs someone else's. Proud Tek is the first kind: we etch or print the antenna, flip-chip bond the [NXP silicon](/about/certifications/), convert the inlay, print your artwork and encode the data, then read-verify each unit before it leaves our [Shenzhen factory](/about/factory/). Start with a [free NFC sample pack](/sample-pack/), or jump to the parts most buyers order — [NTAG 213 NFC stickers](/products/rfid-labels/ntag213-nfc-sticker/). The numbers below are the ones a procurement team checks first.
bullets: Full form-factor range from one line — paper and PET stickers, wet and dry inlays on rolls, epoxy hard tags, anti-metal tags and tamper-evident labels — so a mixed NFC program ships against one purchase order, not five.

Own-the-line process — antenna etching and printing, flip-chip bonding, reel-to-reel converting, offset and screen printing and inline encoding all happen in-house, so lead time and quality are ours to control, not a subcontractor's.

NXP-allocated silicon — we run NTAG 213/215/216, NTAG 424 DNA, MIFARE Ultralight and ICODE SLIX2 from NXP and NXP-authorised distribution, with STMicroelectronics ST25TA and Fudan compatibles offered only where a program is explicitly cost-driven.

Converter- and integrator-ready output — inlays delivered on rolls in standard pitches for label converters, tags supplied bare for lamination, and print-and-encode stickers finished to your artwork from a 25 mm round inlay up.
Compliance manufactured in, not bolted on — RoHS, REACH SVHC, CE and FCC material and radio declarations per shipment, with quality records retained seven years under ISO 9001.

bullets: NTAG 213 — {chip:nxp-ntag-213:user_bytes} bytes user memory, NFC Forum Type 2 tag, ideal for URL encoding, product authentication and marketing stickers where cost efficiency matters.
NTAG 215 — {chip:nxp-ntag-215:user_bytes} bytes user memory, commonly used for gaming NFC (Amiibo compatible), loyalty programs and applications needing more data storage.
NTAG 216 — {chip:nxp-ntag-216:user_bytes} bytes user memory, the largest NTAG chip for vCard storage, complex NDEF records and multi-record applications.

NTAG 424 DNA — AES-128 mutual authentication with a SUN (Secure Unique NFC) message that generates a fresh cryptographic code on every tap, for anti-counterfeit and cloud-verified product authentication (NFC Forum Type 4).
MIFARE Ultralight EV1 — up to 128 bytes user memory with an originality signature and one-time-programmable counters, for single-use tickets, transit fares and event access.
ICODE SLIX2 — an ISO/IEC 15693 vicinity chip at 13.56 MHz built for longer HF read range in library media and industrial-automation tagging.

sections.title: Inside the line: how an NFC tag is manufactured
sections.intro: A datasheet makes an NFC tag look like one part; the factory floor knows it is five. Here is how a bare NXP wafer becomes an encoded, read-tested tag on our line — antenna first, silicon second, and the QC read-test that decides whether a unit ships at all. Nothing in this sequence is subcontracted to a job shop, which is why a program that mixes form factors can still ship on one [production traveler](/about/factory/).

image.alt: Five in-house manufacturing stages left to right. Stage 1, antenna: aluminium or copper antenna etched or printed on a PET or paper web. Stage 2, chip bonding: NXP silicon flip-chip bonded to the antenna to form the inlay. Stage 3, converting: wet and dry inlays laminated and die-cut on rolls, reel-to-reel. Stage 4, printing and finishing: offset and screen artwork, lamination, epoxy and molding. Stage 5, encoding and QC: NDEF or SUN records written, then every unit 100% read-tested. A base arrow runs from a bare wafer, in-house, to a shipped SKU under one QC sign-off.

items.label: 1. Antenna
items.text: The aluminium or copper antenna is etched or printed onto a PET or paper web and matched to the target chip and surface — the geometry that decides read range is set here, not bought off a shelf.

items.label: 2. Chip bonding
items.text: NXP wafers are flip-chip bonded to the antenna to form the inlay, with an originality-signature check so the silicon on the line is the silicon on the quote.

items.label: 3. Converting
items.text: Inlays are laminated wet or dry and die-cut to size, delivered on continuous rolls in standard pitches for label converters or singulated for hard-tag assembly.

items.label: 4. Printing & finishing
items.text: Full-colour artwork is offset-, screen- or digitally printed and laminated; epoxy and anti-metal tags are domed or molded into their housings.

items.label: 5. Encoding & QC
items.text: NDEF records or NTAG 424 DNA SUN messages are written inline, every unit is 100% read-tested, and a batch report with chip response and read-range data ships with the order.

sections.title: OEM/ODM and factory-direct: what owning the line unlocks
sections.intro: Most NFC brands in Europe and North America already buy from Shenzhen and add a margin on the way to you; buying factory-direct simply removes the middle. Owning the line is also what makes real OEM/ODM possible — your brand on the tag, your antenna tuned to your surface, your encoding scheme locked on the traveler — instead of a logo printed on someone's stock part. For a worked example, see [NFC brand authentication](/solutions/nfc-brand-authentication/).

Prototype NFC tags in 5-7 days, because sampling runs on the same line that will make the volume order.
Stickers, inlays, epoxy and anti-metal tags from one line, one MOQ conversation, one documentation pack.
A named account contact through reorders, with your artwork and encoding scheme on file for instant repeats.

bullets: OEM and ODM white-label — we manufacture under your brand with your artwork and packaging, or develop a tag to your functional spec from scratch; no Proud Tek marking appears unless you want it.
Full customization — antenna size and shape, chip selection, substrate, adhesive, printing, encoding and packaging are all specified by you, because we control every step that sets them.

Custom antenna and inlay development — where a catalogue inlay will not tune to your surface (glass, metal, a curved bottle), our RF engineers design and prototype a new antenna against your real material.

Everything below is verifiable before you commit — the [certifications page](/about/certifications/) shows each standard and how to confirm it with the registrar, and the [factory page](/about/factory/) documents the plant behind the tags.

faq.question: How do I verify an NFC tag factory in China before ordering?
faq.answer: Three independent checks. Request our ISO 9001, ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 certificate numbers and confirm them with the issuing registrar; book a factory audit — in person or virtual — at our Shenzhen operation; and order a free sample kit to read the tags on your own phones and readers. Every batch also ships with a test report showing chip response, resonance frequency and read range, and we accommodate SGS, TUV or Intertek inspection when a program requires it.

faq.question: Do you manufacture OEM and ODM NFC tags under our brand?
faq.answer: Yes — OEM and ODM are the core of what a factory does. For OEM we build to your drawings and print your artwork and packaging with no Proud Tek marking; for ODM we develop a tag to your functional spec — chip, antenna, substrate and encoding — from scratch. Your design files and encoding scheme are locked on the production traveler and kept on file so reorders are identical.

faq.question: Can you design a custom antenna or inlay for our surface?
faq.answer: Yes. Where a catalogue inlay will not tune to your material — glass, metal, a curved bottle or a small on-metal footprint — our RF engineers design a new antenna and prototype it against your real surface and reader, typically in 5-7 days, then read-range test it before the antenna is committed to tooling.

faq.question: Can you supply NFC tags pre-encoded and locked?
faq.answer: Yes. We write NDEF records — static or UID-personalised URLs, vCards, Wi-Fi credentials or app-launch records — inline during production, and can lock pages read-only after encoding so the data cannot be overwritten. For NTAG 424 DNA we configure the SUN mirror and your backend URL so each tap produces a fresh cryptographic signature. Every encoded unit is 100% read-verified.

faq.question: What are your NFC tag manufacturing MOQs, and can I sample first?
faq.answer: Free samples come first: 5-10 encoded tags of any type so you can test before you buy. For production, printed NFC stickers start around 500 pieces, wet or dry inlay rolls around 1,000 pieces, and epoxy or hard tags around 200 pieces, with plain stock tags from 100 pieces for pilots — but the exact minimum depends on chip, size and encoding, so we quote it per program. Send your spec and target volume for written MOQ and pricing.

faq.question: Do you manufacture NFC inlays on rolls for label converters?
faq.answer: Yes. We manufacture wet inlays on continuous rolls with standard pitch spacing (16 mm, 18 mm or custom) compatible with major converting lines from Mühlbauer, Melzer and BIELOMATIK, in narrow-web (50-80 mm) and wide-web (200-320 mm) widths. Tell us your converting equipment and we match the pitch and web width to it.
